text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Fifty Moslems were expelled over the weekend from the village of Kopice, near the central town of Maglaj, by Croat police after authorities from nearby Croat-held Zepce allowed the Moslems to return to the village and repair their houses, witnesses say. The police were led by Anto Marincic, a deputy in the Moslem- Croat federation parliament.

- Pre-war occupants of flats in the Moslem-Croat federation who left and spent the war in Bosnia's Serb territory can buy the flats under a proposed privatisation law but only if citizens from the federation have the same right in the Serb republic, says federation official.

- Those with apartments that are officially described as abandoned will not have a right to buy them, federation official says. According to the law, a flat is considered abandoned if an owner is absent for six months without reason.

- The Serb Civic Council calls for amendments to constitution that would grant Serbs, Croats and Moslems equal rights in both of the country's entities. Serbs in the Moslem-Croat federation or Croats and Moslems in the Serb republic should not be treated as minorities or second-class citizens.

- A group of Moslems visited the Serb-controlled town of Trebinje for the first time since Moslems were expelled from the town at the beginning of the war. They toured cemeteries but were prevented from meeting their pre-war Serb neighbours because police dispersed a Serb crowd. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387 71 663 864
